# API Contract Maintenance

TDNS keeps its HTTP contract and generated clients in the repository. The
Swaggo annotations are the source of truth; generated Swagger, OpenAPI, Go, and
TypeScript files must not be edited by hand.

## Source and Generated Files

| Ownership | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source | `api/annotations.go` | API metadata, security scheme, and shared Swaggo definitions |
| Source | `internal/httpapi/handlers_*.go` | Operation annotations next to server-only handlers |
| Source | `api/dto.go` | Request and response wire types referenced by annotations |
| Source | `internal/httpapi/handler.go` | Route registration and optional Swagger endpoints |
| Generated | `api/docs/` | Swaggo's Go registration package and Swagger 2.0 JSON/YAML |
| Generated | `api/openapi.yaml` | OpenAPI 3.0 contract converted from Swagger 2.0 |
| Generated | `apiclient/generated/` | Public Go transport generated by oapi-codegen |
| Generated | `web/app/generated/` | TypeScript API definitions generated by openapi-typescript |

Security-related contract changes are sequenced in
`docs/security-plan.md`. They must follow the same generation and drift checks
described here.

## Regeneration

Regenerate all API artifacts:

```bash
./tools/generate_api.sh
```

The script formats and runs Swaggo, lints the Swagger contract, converts it to
OpenAPI 3.0, lints the converted contract, and generates both clients. Go
generator versions are pinned in `tools/generate_api.sh`; Node generator
versions are pinned in `web/package-lock.json`. On a clean checkout, the script
installs the locked Node dependencies automatically.

Run the complete local CI gate from a clean working tree with one command:

```bash
./tools/verify.sh
```

This regenerates the API artifacts, rejects tracked or untracked drift in the
generated paths, runs Go and web tests, checks TypeScript, and builds the static
web application through `tools/generate_web.sh`. Commit source and generated
contract changes together.

## Swagger UI

Swagger endpoints are disabled by default. Enable them in `tdns.yaml` or the
active server configuration:

```yaml
server:
  swagger_enabled: true
```

The server then exposes:

- `/swagger/` for Swagger UI
- `/swagger/doc.json` for Swagger 2.0 JSON
- `/swagger/openapi.yaml` for OpenAPI 3.0 YAML

Protected operations use the same bearer token as the REST API. In Swagger UI,
enter the complete `Bearer <token>` value in the authorization dialog. Keep the
Swagger endpoints disabled on installations where interactive API discovery is
not required.

Management bearer tokens have either `tdns.kubewire.net:ro` or
`tdns.kubewire.net:rw` scope. Read-write tokens may call every protected route;
read-only tokens are limited to query and status operations. Generated clients
continue to send the token through the `Authorization` header and receive
`403 Forbidden` when an authenticated token lacks the required scope.

## Client Boundaries

The importable Go client is `github.com/jfardello/tdns/apiclient`. Its generated
transport and schema types live under `apiclient/generated`; handwritten
configuration, authentication, and compatibility helpers stay in the parent
package. Do not add application policy to generated files.

The public `api` package owns DTOs and the embedded OpenAPI contract. The
server-only implementation belongs to `internal/httpapi`, while `resolver`
owns DNS upstream transport. These boundaries prevent management HTTP code and
DNS transport code from sharing an ambiguous `client` package name.

The web application imports generated definitions from
`web/app/generated/api.d.ts`. Runtime requests go through
`web/app/lib/apiClient.ts` and the Nuxt adapter in
`web/app/composables/useApiClient.ts`; components and domain composables should
not recreate endpoint or response types manually.

When an API change cannot be represented accurately by the generators, fix the
annotations or DTO boundary first. Do not patch generated output as a permanent
solution.
